feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications role: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership over major digital channels, governance, and platform modernization.  
- Good credibility through specific tools and scale indicators: 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, GA4/BigQuery/Power BI stack.  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with strong clarity around cross-channel communications, advocacy messaging, and technical/content translation.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: e.g., engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption improvements, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and avoid a repetitive feel.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with a clearer leadership angle and a few more distinctive, recent signals from your NACo and consulting work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your current level and niche: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Add one or two concrete differentiators, such as Drupal/web transformation, analytics-informed strategy, or advocacy-focused digital programs.
- Tighten phrasing by reducing broad lists like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs.”

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial and operational workflow design, and audience-focused content strategy across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/system language closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and leaning toward higher-value, less generic capabilities will make it feel more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Web/CMS administration • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & automation • Stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Replace “multi-channel communication” with “cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Change “workflow & systems architecture” to “workflow architecture & automation” if you want better alignment with Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier in later sections.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; “Web & CMS administration” and “Policy & advocacy communication” are good, but ensure all items follow the same style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming to 6–8 items or using it only for broad themes not listed elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and “Recent Projects.” Make it sharper by foregrounding ownership, platform scale, and any early outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Advised,” “Launched.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages/templates/toolkits launched, stakeholders supported, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, or traffic/member usage.
- Example rewrite: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative across legislative/member content, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX to improve findability on high-volume public web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the Drupal microsite work are already covered in Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on role-level ownership, scale, and outcomes.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the summary and NACo roles; avoid repeating generic platform-management language.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize transformation outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific or measurable: include subscriber growth, engagement, campaign performance, production volume, or cost/time savings if available.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve executive visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and infrastructure.
- “Governance/publishing standards” may echo the current consulting role; distinguish with NACo-specific scale or organizational change.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operating ownership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the higher-level strategy/governance work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize executional leadership: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social, and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scope: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and include views, open rates, engagement, or production cadence if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this as scaling/operationalizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership and governance rather than broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented skill labels:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & workflow design
- Cross-channel communications operations leadership
- Public-sector advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered content planning & information architecture
- Use “operations,” “workflow design,” and “information architecture” to signal systems leadership, not just messaging.
- Drop generic wording like “multi-channel communications leadership” unless paired with “operations” or “governance.”
- If space allows, align phrasing with recent work by foregrounding web modernization and AI/search-adjacent content systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is weaker and more generic than the stronger experience-based positioning elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. In Topline Skills, this should signal current platform depth and execution strengths, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Refocus on higher-value, recent capabilities: “Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here: remove jQuery and Airtable systems from this topline line; keep them in Technical + IT if needed.
- Consider grouping by capability rather than platform list: “Enterprise CMS platforms (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • Front-end implementation • Integrations & automation • AI-enabled search”
- If possible, align wording to proven impact from recent roles/projects, e.g., “Drupal modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Platform/tool specifics are also repeated in Technical + IT; Topline Skills should stay more selective.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting”
- Group tools more tightly and cut redundancy: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, stronger phrasing such as “search, UX and performance optimization”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • Search, UX and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording duplicates the “Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use one strategic phrase here and leave tool detail to Technical + IT

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and tied to recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Hybrid Events
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, add one impact cue in the section intro or elsewhere, e.g. “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast-quality studio” to connect skills to proven delivery.
- Consider dropping “virtual” if “hybrid event production” already covers it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Tool-level detail like PTZ may be better in Technical + IT unless it supports a clear leadership/operations positioning here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This item should either add nuance (level/scope) or be tightened to avoid repeating the same platform list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to a scoped skills line, e.g.: “Enterprise CMS & web platforms: Drupal (primary), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Put Drupal first and mark it as primary, since recent roles and projects are heavily Drupal-centered.
- If space allows, add level/context instead of more tools: “Drupal (site migration, microsites, governance), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not materially supported elsewhere; it reads lighter than the enterprise platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; keep one list broader and the other more contextual.
- Avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint in multiple sections without adding proficiency or business impact.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in current Drupal work.
- If space allows, add context instead of only tools: Front-end implementation, tag management, serverless scripting, CI/CD automation, and API-based integrations
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add light impact framing: supported Drupal microsites, analytics deployments, and workflow automation for large public-facing platforms

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM also overlaps with analytics infrastructure in recent roles; keep it here only if positioned as hands-on implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems-building, not just apps: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming the category to: “Workflow Automation, Collaboration & Project Systems”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: “Airtable (database/workflow design) • Power Automate, Zapier (process automation) • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp (project coordination) • Slack, Microsoft Teams (team operations)”
- Prioritize tools tied to recent work and drop weaker/older items if needed; Basecamp or Trello may be least essential.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are collaboration tools, so this section should not overclaim automation unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown in recent roles: leading large-scale email/newsletter operations. It should signal platform depth and audience/automation use, not just list vendor names.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email newsletter operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation”
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented: “Email & Engagement Systems: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp; newsletter operations for tens of thousands of recipients; audience segmentation and journey automation.”
- Keep naming consistent and concise: use either “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys” or the current product name used elsewhere in your materials, but avoid slashes if they may confuse ATS parsing.
- Prioritize capabilities tied to recent work: segmentation, automation, campaign operations, and stakeholder/member communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience.
- Don’t add “social” or “analytics” here; those are already well represented in other skills sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale or output metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add specific execution scope: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “coordinated the work of a digital media associate” or “mentored a junior digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume, audience growth, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” repeats the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early producing, not expanding.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive “firsts” and cross-functional coordination rather than broad digital production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities, while helping translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten it: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how content advanced advocacy/program goals.
- Remove vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with specific outputs or teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; keep this positioned as a coordination/innovation role with an early content milestone.
